sources.title: Bringing Up a Chip on the Cheap
sources.what_it_covers: Real silicon bring-up war story for the Stanford Smart Memories research chip. Covers power-on failures, JTAG/debug issues, memory BIST problems, FPGA-based bring-up platform, and lessons learned from getting first silicon working with minimal custom hardware.
sources.why_relevant: Detailed first-hand account of failure-and-recovery during research chip bring-up, including specific debug steps that failed and what worked.
sources.verification_hint: DOI 10.1109/MDT.2011.2179849 or search IEEE Xplore for Wachs Shacham Asgar Firoozshahian Richardson Horowitz chip cheap

sources.title: Challenges in Achieving First-Silicon Success for 10M-Gate SoCs: A Silicon Engineering Perspective
sources.what_it_covers: Cadence/Simplex perspective on physical design failures for multi-million-gate SoCs: interconnect modeling gaps, physical re-synthesis, IR-drop analysis, crosstalk prevention, and the gap between tool promises and silicon reality. Based on 23 real tape-outs.
sources.why_relevant: Direct practitioner account of systematic failure modes in large ASIC physical design — routing congestion, timing correlation, and methodology traps at 10M-gate scale.
sources.verification_hint: DAC 39th accepted papers list, Special Session, 2002, or IEEE eWh page for Aurangzeb Khan IEEE SSCS Santa Clara Valley 2003 expanded version

sources.title: How VLSI Monks Successfully Resolved Timing Closure Challenges in Advanced Node Physical Design
sources.what_it_covers: Real engagement postmortem: 7nm FinFET high-performance ASIC with severe setup violations, routing congestion, clock skew, hold violations, and signal EM issues. Documents the full structured fix cycle from diagnosis through sign-off STA closure.
sources.why_relevant: Detailed war-story-style account of modern advanced-node timing closure failure and recovery, covering critical-path optimization, congestion reduction, CTS balancing, hold fixing, and ECO-based fixes.
sources.verification_hint: site:vlsimonks.com timing closure advanced node physical design 2026

sources.title: Lessons from Silicon – A Critical Tapeout Experience
sources.venue_or_publication: LinkedIn (Sourav Banerjee, Intel Physical Design Manager)
sources.what_it_covers: First-hand postmortem: a large CPU core tapeout that powered on successfully but exhibited intermittent OS reboots traced to a noise violation in a memory cache — missed due to overly optimistic memory models during sign-off. Required metal ECO with spacing and shielding in the subsequent stepping.
sources.why_relevant: Real post-silicon failure-and-recovery story from an industrial CPU physical design lead: noise/margin escape that survived pre-silicon sign-off, and the cross-functional debug process that found it.
sources.verification_hint: LinkedIn post by Sourav Banerjee physical design Lessons from Silicon Critical Tapeout 2025

sources.title: Performance Verification of the AmpereOne CPU Core
sources.what_it_covers: Industrial-scale PV methodology for Ampere's custom CPU across four generations. Includes a documented first-silicon escape: a BTB sign-extension logic bug that caused mispredictions for kernel-address-space code, caught post-silicon because EL1 test coverage was missing. Also documents an MTE-related store-to-load forwarding issue fixed in gen-2 silicon.
sources.why_relevant: Rare published account of a specific first-silicon performance escape in an industrial ARM-compatible server CPU — root cause traced to a gap in pre-silicon test coverage, with explicit recovery via next-stepping.
sources.verification_hint: arXiv:2608.19300 or search AmpereOne performance verification BTB first silicon August 2026

sources.title: First-Silicon Power-on Checklist and Day-0 Triage
sources.what_it_covers: Structured bring-up failure taxonomy: power sequencing failures, JTAG/scan chain failures, clock bring-up failures, memory init failures, and debug transport failures. Includes case study of a program that recovered a week of schedule by standardizing board setup metadata before expanding debug branches. Documents the triage decision tree and evidence capture discipline.
sources.why_relevant: Real failure-and-recovery patterns from industrial silicon bring-up, with explicit case studies on how wrong assumptions about board debug domains caused misdiagnosed failures. War-story density despite the structured format.
sources.verification_hint: site:densechip.com first-silicon checklist day-0 triage bring-up
